description: Python SDK (cachekit-py) auto-mode storage container: CK v3 frame. Python-SDK-internal — other SDKs identify and reject, never decode. See spec/wire-format.md 'SDK Storage Containers (auto mode)'.
frame_layout: MAGIC 'CK' (0x43 0x4B) | VERSION u8 (0x03) | HDR_LEN u32 big-endian | HEADER (UTF-8 JSON: {s, m, v}) | PAYLOAD (raw bytes)

frame_vectors.name: default_saas_write_msgpack_bytestorage
frame_vectors.description: Exact stored bytes for a default @cache write (StandardSerializer, integrity on): CK v3 frame wrapping the ByteStorage envelope of the MessagePack-encoded value. This is what any backend — including the SaaS — receives from cachekit-py in auto mode.

frame_vectors.name: arrow_dataframe_write
frame_vectors.description: DataFrame write via ArrowSerializer: CK v3 frame wrapping the Arrow envelope [8-byte xxHash3-64 checksum][Arrow IPC file]. Arrow IPC bytes are NOT canonical across pyarrow versions (this vector: pyarrow 25.0.0) — verify frame structure and envelope detection only, never IPC bytes.

frame_vectors.name: default_saas_write_msgpack_bytestorage_bin
frame_vectors.description: Default @cache write (StandardSerializer, integrity on) from a protocol 1.1 wheel: the ByteStorage envelope's compressed_data is msgpack bin (serde_bytes) instead of the legacy array of integers. Readers MUST accept both encodings; the legacy encoding stays pinned by default_saas_write_msgpack_bytestorage. When this vector carries 'twin_of', that field — not this text — is the claim that the two differ only in envelope encoding, and verify enforces it.

payload_envelope.encoding: rmp_serde positional fixarray(4); compressed_data encodes as msgpack bin (serde_bytes, protocol 1.1); checksum [u8;8] stays an array of integers
